title: Ministries 2 of 4: a leader on the phone, and joining
question: Lay leaders without a desktop: asks to answer, the team and attendee lists (each child with their parents), settings, posting, teams under their ministry. Joining: a visitor, a parent for their child, a young person. Which should I build?

options.label: A People tab with two lists
options.thesis: Leaders get a People tab: Team and Attendees, asks on top, a sheet per person.
options.viewport: People tab on Attendees: two asking, then each child with their parents and a flag when none is linked; a sheet to link a parent, move to the team or stop attending; Settings as a ⚙ tab; joining asks who for: Mia to attend, or me on the team.
options.risk: Two extra tabs for leaders on a narrow phone.

options.label: Everything in place
options.lineage: a noticeboard you pin straight onto
options.thesis: No leader tabs: asks and the team on About, Edit turns the page into a form, Post floats on News.
options.viewport: About shows asks waiting and the team with Add; Edit from the top bar; News has a floating Post; joining asks which team.
options.risk: About gets long for leaders; attendees and parents have no home.

options.label: Compose first
options.lineage: a leader's notebook open at a fresh page
options.thesis: A leader's ministry opens on a box to write in, then what's waiting.
options.viewport: A box to write in with Post, Event, File; Waiting on you (asks, no parent linked); Team, Attendees, Settings rows; the post sheet with audience chips and how many an important post reaches.
options.risk: Leaders look after people more often than they post.
